(as an idle side note, the following scenario happened recently...)

a Turbo-Baron variant as my prey with a full Baron up first.

My Krassimir up with a Masquer and Guardian Angel attached, along with
Cameron and Paul diCarlo.

Baron attempts to get the Soul Gem, blocked by Krassimir with help from
the Baron's prey playing Draba after the stealth modifier. Krassimir
extracts a Signpost from his wallet, backhands 6 blood off the Baron and
Disarms him into torpor -- Paul bleeds, Cameron eats the Baron protected
by the Edge and gets a NEC skill card.

Soul Gem and Baron *both* in ash heap = bad things, man.

Fast-forward several turns... Carlotta has come out, retrieved the Soul
Gem with her ability, equipped it, and Possessed the Baron back into
play. Krassimir has gotten a NEC skill card. Baron attempts to get the
Soul Gem... gets blocked by Krassimir with superior Spectral Divination
and nudged into torpor again. Carlotta eats the Baron... and burns
because I still had the Edge. Oops. Fortunately, Rudolfo Giovanni is
the crypt-topper and comes out, so the Soul Gem is not lost to the ash
heap.

Rudy successfully Possesses the Baron, the Baron gets the Soul Gem, and
Force of Wills at inferior for a bleed of 3. Hurray! The Baron poofs,
and Gisela Harden comes out full. No Possessions in hand at the moment,
but still in decent shape overall, right?

Comes around to my turn? Krassimir Daemonically Possesses the Baron.

Some days just aren't good days for sleaze... =)

Messages.Author: Ben Peal
Messages.Body:
LSJ wrote:
> Ben Peal wrote:
> > LSJ wrote:
> > > The Archon loophole, not Tyler, is on the list for RT review.
> >
> > Is the Soul Gem of Etrius likewise up for RT review? (see: Turbo Arika)
>
> It has been reviewed several times already, yes.

Ah, ok.

> Do you feel something has been missed or that the situation for Soul Gem
> has changed?

Not at all. I was just curious as to whether it was reviewed at all,
as it seemed to be of the same ilk as Archon in terms of its potential
for looping.

> Or do you feel that things should not be reviewed until they are proven
> to be broken?

I'm torn on it, really. On one hand, I'm of the opinion that the game
should be left alone unless a problem arises. On the other hand, I
appreciate the diligence of the Rules Team, and the efforts towards
preventative maintainance. :)

In the case of Archon and Soul Gem, my feeling on them is that the
No Repeat Actions rules were created to prevent looping (please
correct me if I'm wrong), and as such, Archon and Soul Gem seem to
violate that notion. So, on one hand, there hasn't yet been a problem
with them, so I'd be inclined to leave them alone. On the other hand,
they seem inconsistent with the development of the game with respect
to No Repeat Actions and looping, so I'd be inclined to change them.

Fortunately, I'm not one of the decision-makers. :)
